newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria's ruling Socialists approve counter-demos.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria's ruling Socialists approve counter-demos.

text.p: Leaders of Bulgaria's ruling Socialists on Wednesday gave approval for local party groups to organise mass protests against opposition rallies now in their 16th day.

"Local party structures should assess the necessity of mass action supporting giving a second mandate to the Left," Valery Radev, regional party leader from the mining town of Bobov Dol, near Sofia, told reporters after a leadership meeting.
Counter-rallies by supporters of neighbouring Serbia's Socialist President Slobodan Milosevic in Belgrade on December 24 led to violent clashes between demonstrators and riot police.
Asked when the counter-demonstrations could begin, Radev said they could start immediately and continue until the Socialists received a mandate to form a new government.

The Socialists have offered elections in December, a year ahead of schedule, but want to form a second cabinet following the resignation of prime minister Zhan Videnov on December 21. The opposition Union of Democratic Forces wants polls in March.
New president Petar Stoyanov, who took office on Wednesday, will hold talks with the two sides on Thursday morning.
